functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population

neuromuscular_junction_zone.location_description: mid-belly endplate band -- for where this band lies along the muscle, see motor_endplate_zones

functional_compartments.function_note: The only long flexor of the thumb; innervated by the anterior interosseous nerve (a pure motor branch of median n., classically tested via the 'OK sign' pinch).
functional_compartments.source: Holzbaur KR, Murray WM, Delp SL (2005) Ann Biomed Eng 33(6):829-840 -- upper-extremity muscle architecture model (fascicle length, pennation, PCSA)

motor_endplate_zones.method: modified Sihler's stain intramuscular nerve-dense region, with muscle-spindle abundance histology
motor_endplate_zones.notes: Nerve-dense region of about 3.32 cm2, supplied by the anterior interosseous nerve. Highest spindle abundance in its LOWER third, at 63.67% of muscle length -- distinctly distal to mid-belly.
motor_endplate_zones.source: Zhou J, Jia F, Chen P, Zhou G, Wang M, Wu J, Yang S, 'Localisation of the centre of the highest region of muscle spindle abundance of anterior forearm muscles', J Anat 244(5):803-814 (2023), doi:10.1111/joa.14000 -- 24 adult cadavers, modified Sihler's staining with muscle-spindle histology and spiral CT localisation

injection_target_points.label: main
injection_target_points.method: modified Sihler's stain intramuscular nerve-dense region, with muscle-spindle abundance histology, localised by spiral CT with barium sulphate labelling
injection_target_points.notes: SURFACE NOT ESTABLISHED. The source places all but one of its eleven projection points on the anterior forearm and one on the posterior forearm, but the label identifying the exception was lost in full-text extraction, so `depth_measured_from` is omitted here rather than guessed. The three percentages are unaffected; confirm the surface against the paper's CT localisation figure before planning a needle path from the depth figure.

ultrasound_injection_approach.transducer_placement: Transverse on the volar forearm, radial side of the distal third, medial to the radial cortex.
ultrasound_injection_approach.depth_layer: Deep layer of the anterior compartment.
ultrasound_injection_approach.notes: The narrowest safety margin in the distal upper limb: the radial artery and median nerve are often less than 1 cm from the target, so ultrasound guidance is not optional here. Injected for the thumb-in-hand deformity, which can otherwise cause palmar ulceration.
ultrasound_injection_approach.source: Diaconu S et al. (Elias University Hospital), 'A Visual Guide to Ultrasound-Guided Botulinum Toxin Injection in Spasticity: Part I -- Distal Upper Limb Muscles', Toxins 17(3):107 (2025), doi:10.3390/toxins17030107

trigger_points.location_description: Belly in the distal half of the radial volar forearm, deep to flexor carpi radialis and brachioradialis, palpated against the radius.
trigger_points.referred_pain_pattern: Palmar aspect of the thumb to the tip of the distal phalanx.
trigger_points.activation_perpetuating_factors: Forceful or sustained pinch (pliers, writing, gaming, needlework), thumb flexion under load.
trigger_points.notes: Non-myofascial differential: trigger thumb, basal-joint arthritis, FCR tendinopathy, De Quervain's disease (dorsoradial), anterior interosseous nerve palsy, C6 radiculopathy.
trigger_points.source: Simons, Travell & Simons (1999) Trigger Point Manual, 2nd ed., Vol. 1, ch. 38; Donnelly et al. (2019) 3rd ed., ch. 38 -- as cited in this atlas's uploaded wrist muscle reference.

clinical.function_biomechanics: Major: Flexion of the thumb IP joint (its sole flexor), then MCP and carpometacarpal flexion–adduction; principal contributor to tip and key pinch force [1, 5]. At the wrist: Weak wrist flexion with slight radial deviation [1, 6]. Coupling: The Linburg–Comstock interconnection couples FPL to the index FDP, causing distal forearm pain and loss of independent thumb flexion when the index finger is held extended [45]. Importance: Pinch and precision handling; restored after loss by brachioradialis or ECRL transfer [4].
clinical.adjacent_structures: Bursae / sheaths: Radial bursa, which communicates with the ulnar bursa at the wrist in a proportion of hands; thumb pulleys A1, oblique, A2 [1, 4]. Relations: Anterior interosseous nerve and artery between FPL and FDP; the tendon lies directly on the volar rim of the distal radius at the watershed line, where prominent volar plates abrade it [46]. Coupled structures: Anterior interosseous nerve, median nerve in the carpal tunnel, volar rim of the distal radius, thumb pulleys [1, 4, 46].

trigger_points.referred_pain: Palmar aspect of the thumb to the tip of the distal phalanx [2, 3].
trigger_points.activation_perpetuating_factors: Forceful or sustained pinch (pliers, writing, gaming, needlework), thumb flexion under load [2, 3].

clinical.pain_referred_into_territory: Pain referred into FPL territory (palmar thumb, radial volar wrist)
clinical.non_myofascial_differential: Trigger thumb, basal-joint arthritis, FCR tendinopathy, De Quervain's disease (dorsoradial), AIN palsy, C6 radiculopathy.
clinical.notes: Attritional rupture over prominent volar locking plates (graded by plate position relative to the watershed line) [46]; anterior interosseous nerve palsy (Kiloh–Nevin) [43]; trigger thumb at the A1 pulley; FPL tenosynovitis; Volkmann's contracture; carpal tunnel syndrome [4].
clinical.caveat: Referred-pain maps from Travell and Simons are clinical consensus drawings, not experimentally derived; the APL and pronator quadratus maps (Hwang et al.) are experimental hypertonic-saline studies in healthy volunteers. Grade C items (Appendix A rows 23, 44–46, 48): TrP distances, muscle-level arterial detail, the ECRL/ECRB insertional bursa, the grip-strength claim for PL agenesis, and the extrapolated EDM/EPB/EPL referral statements. All are labelled in the text. Referred-pain conventions. "TrP referral" is the essential (dark) zone described by Travell and Simons unless "spillover" is stated. TrP locations in centimetres are approximations read from the Manual's figures and should be confirmed by palpation of the taut band. Quantitative biomechanical values are cadaveric means and vary with forearm rotation and wrist angle.
